title: Article 21: From Gopalan to Maneka

endcard.line: Pictures: MohitSingh (CC BY 3.0); Beohar Rammanohar Sinha (public domain)

segments.say: Article twenty-one is one sentence long. No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Its meaning has grown enormously.

items.text: Any procedure in a valid law is enough

segments.say: In nineteen fifty, in the Gopalan case, the Supreme Court read it narrowly. If a law laid down a procedure, that was enough, fair or not.
Then came the Emergency, and a bitter lesson about how easily liberty could be taken.

items.text: The procedure must be fair, just and reasonable

segments.say: In nineteen seventy-eight, the Maneka Gandhi case changed everything. The Court said the procedure itself must be fair, just and reasonable, and that rights must be read together.
Since then, 'life' has come to mean a life with dignity: livelihood, clean environment, speedy trial, legal aid, and in twenty seventeen, privacy.
In one line: from 'any law will do' to 'the law must be fair', close to what Americans call due process.
For GS Two: Gopalan, narrow. Maneka, fair, just and reasonable. Puttaswamy, privacy. That's the story of Article twenty-one.

sources: A.K. Gopalan v State of Madras, AIR 1950 SC 27: 'procedure established by law' means procedure in an enacted law; rights read in isolation
Maneka Gandhi v Union of India (1978) 1 SCC 248: procedure must be fair, just and reasonable; Articles 14, 19 and 21 interlinked
Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v Union of India (2017) 10 SCC 1: right to privacy protected under Article 21
Olga Tellis (1985, livelihood), Hussainara Khatoon (1979, speedy trial), Subhash Kumar (1991, clean environment): widening of Article 21
